U0500.d: The public code lists checked do not carry U0500 at all, so neither its status as a generic code nor its wording can be confirmed. In the generic numbering, an invalid-data code usually mirrors the lost-communication code of the same module 0x301 lower (U0200 to U0501, U0199 to U049A); for U0500 that partner would be U01FF, which is not assigned in those lists either, so a reserved slot is likely.
s: Code present without any noticeable fault
Remote app, emergency call or online services unavailable (if it concerns the telematics unit)
c: Code read with a manufacturer-specific definition that differs from the generic list
Scan tool decoding the stored fault number incorrectly
Telematics or communication unit sending corrupted frames (analogy to U0499)

U0501.d: Many cars give each door its own electronics: a door unit receives commands over CAN and drives window lift, lock and mirror, as a Yazaki patent describes with a LIN sub-bus inside the door. Module A has its invalid-data code in U049A; U0501 is the same check for the second door unit.
s: One door not following central locking
Window, mirror or door-ajar display of that door erratic
c: Water ingress into the door module through a failed door membrane
Broken wires in the harness grommet between body and door
Door module not programmed or configured after replacement

U0502.d: For door control module C the letter is a weak guide. In the generic list its lost-communication partner is U0201, yet GM's 2011 Saab 9-5 code list uses U0201 for the transfer case control module.
s: Lock, window or mirror of one door working only sometimes
Stored code without noticeable fault
c: Door control module C internally faulty
Damaged wiring in the door hinge area
Manufacturer uses this code slot for another module

U0503.d: U0503 is the invalid-data code for door control module D. It is rarely seen in published service material: Ford, the most visible user of lettered door modules, labels the latch controllers of its four-door electronic-latch cars E to H (DCME–DCMH, e.g.
s: One door not unlocking or locking with the others
Window switch on that door ignored
c: Door control module D internally faulty or water-damaged
Broken data lead in the door harness grommet
Weak 12 V battery causing faulty frames during wake-up

U0504.d: U0504 is the one door code of this series with a public manufacturer case. Ford names the electronic door latch controllers DCME to DCMH, and its programming applications list DCME as door control module E.
s: Door fault warning in the cluster
Transmission Not In Park or Hill Start Assist Not Available messages (Lincoln)
Door latch or electronic door release erratic
c: Door latch module software (Lincoln Aviator/Nautilus, update DCME–DCMH)
Door control module E internally faulty
Damaged wiring between body and door

U0505.d: At Ford, F is the second of the electronic latch modules (DCMF). Its typical troubles are documented, though not with U0505 itself: 2020–2023 Aviators logged latch circuit codes in DCME–DCMH when low battery voltage met fault thresholds set too low (SSM 50556), and Mach-E cars raised false alarms through latch module software (SSM 51292).
s: Door ajar or door fault warning
False alarm after locking
c: Low 12 V battery voltage disturbing the latch module (Ford/Lincoln)
Door control module F internally faulty

U0506.d: G is the seventh door slot and in practice belongs to cars that number their door electronics from E upwards. Ford does so with DCMG, the third of four latch modules in Mach-E, Aviator and Nautilus; Ford service messages name DCMG together with its siblings whenever latch software is updated.
s: Door not opening with the electronic handle
Door fault message in the cluster
c: Latch module software needing update (Ford DCMG)
Weak 12 V supply during locking or wake-up
Door control module G internally faulty

U0507.d: The folding top control module runs the power soft top or retractable hardtop of a convertible: it moves the top through hydraulics or motors, watches latch and position sensors and blocks the sequence when something is in the way. Other units need its status, for example to drop the windows, warn while driving or release the trunk lid.
s: Top refuses to open or close or stops midway
Top not secure warning while driving
c: Top control module software error (BMW F33/F83 example)
Damaged wiring to top position or latch sensors in the folding area
Water reaching the module from a leaking top drain

U0508.d: The moveable roof control module drives an electric sunroof or panoramic glass panel, typically through a cable-driven motor with stored end positions and pinch protection. GM uses the same module name: its Saab 9-5 code list files the loss of contact with this module as U0207, the partner of this code.
s: Sunroof stuck, moving jerkily or one-touch function lost
Roof not closing with the remote key
c: Roof module software or lost initialisation of end positions
Water damage from blocked roof drains
Damaged wiring or connector in the headliner

U0509.d: Seat control module A is usually the electronics of the first powered seat, often the driver's memory seat. The Saab 9-5 code list published by GM spells this out: there, the lost-communication partner U0208 is the memory seat control module.
s: Seat memory positions not recalled
Seat heating or ventilation unavailable
c: Seat module configuration or software not matching the vehicle
Under-seat harness or connector damaged by seat travel or objects
Seat control module A internally faulty

U050A.d: For seat control module B there is a fairly clear manufacturer assignment. Ford calls the front passenger seat unit SCMB, for example in the 2024–2026 Lincoln Nautilus, where it held B120A:2A with an inoperative heated seat (SSM 54647), while the driver side is the DSM.
s: Passenger seat heating or adjustment not working
Seat settings missing in the center display
c: Seat module configuration lost or wrong after programming (Ford SCMB)
Harness under the passenger seat pinched or connector loose
Seat control module B internally faulty

U050B.d: A second moveable roof module only makes sense where the roof has more than one powered element, for instance a sliding front glass panel plus a separately driven rear panel or sunshade, or a large panoramic roof split into sections. U050B records that data from this second unit reached the network but was unusable.
s: Rear roof panel or shade not moving while the front one works
Panel stopping part-way
c: Second roof drive lost its end-position learning
Moveable roof control module B faulty, often after water entry
Connector or lead to the rear roof drive damaged

U050C.d: Door control module H, the last door slot, is used by Ford in two different ways. In the Mach-E, Aviator and Nautilus it is the fourth electronic latch module, DCMH, updated together with DCME–DCMG.
s: Power sliding door moving only partly or not at all
Door ajar or door fault message
c: Power sliding door latch or adjustment fault feeding wrong states (Ford Transit)
Worn wiring in the sliding door track or hinge

U050D.d: The wireless accessory charging module is the inductive pad for phones, almost always following the Qi standard, which Toyota was first to offer from the factory, on the 2013 Avalon. The module reports charging state, phone detection and faults to the infotainment or body controller, which shows the charging icon.
s: Phone not charging on the pad or charging icon missing
Repeated phone position warnings
c: Charging module software outdated or mismatched
Module overheating, e.g. blocked fan or foreign object on the pad
Wireless charging module A internally faulty

U050E.d: U050E belongs to a second inductive charging pad, found in cars that offer one pad up front and another for the rear seats or a second front position. Each pad runs its own transmitter coil, object detection and temperature monitoring, so a fault in B leaves pad A working.
s: Second charging pad inactive while the first works
No charging indication for the rear or second pad
c: Metal object or card on the second pad triggering protection
Software of charging module B not matching the vehicle
Wireless charging module B internally faulty

U0511.d: Seat control module C usually serves a seat beyond the two front ones. GM's Saab 9-5 code list assigns the partner slot U0210 to the rear seat heating control module, and Ford labels its rear seat electronics with later letters altogether (SCMK and SCML for the second-row power seats of the 2025 Navigator, SCMJ for the third-row fold module), so module C is anything but uniform.
s: Rear seat heating not switching on
Power folding or adjustment of a rear seat inoperative
c: Harness pinched by rear seat folding or rail mechanism
Configuration of the rear seat module missing after replacement
Seat control module C internally faulty

U0512.d: U0512 has a documented GM case that goes beyond comfort functions. On the 2020 Cadillac CT5 with option UGN, the image processing module, which handles camera data for driver assistance, could set U0512 and display Service Driver Assist.
s: Service Driver Assist message (Cadillac CT5)
Driver assistance features temporarily unavailable
Seat functions served by module D not responding
c: Software in the receiving module (Cadillac CT5 image processing module)
Seat module D configuration or software mismatch
Damaged harness or connector under the seat

U0513.d: A yaw rate sensor reports how quickly the body rotates about its vertical axis, and stability control weighs that rotation against steering angle, wheel speeds and sideways acceleration. U0513 means frames from a separate yaw rate sensor module do arrive, but the receiver rejects them: value out of range, invalid-status bit, wrong counter or checksum.
s: ESC/stability control and traction control warning lamps on
Stability control interventions unavailable
Driver assistance relying on vehicle motion data switched off
c: Sensor element drifting or giving an offset the receiver flags as implausible
Loose mounting or corroded connector at the sensor module
Sensor module or brake controller software/configuration not matching after replacement
Disturbed CAN signals (wiring, terminating resistor, interference)

U0514.d: J2012 provides two mirror control units, and U0514 concerns unit A: its frames keep arriving, but the receiver finds the content unusable, for instance a signal flagged invalid, a wrong counter or checksum, or a value outside the defined range. FCA ties the letter to the cabin mirror.
s: Often no noticeable effect; code found only during a scan
Auto-dimming or camera mirror view unavailable
Mirror memory or folding function not working
c: Software error in the mirror module sending invalid signal values
Vehicle configuration in the BCM not matching the fitted mirror variant
Mirror control module A internally faulty
Loose or corroded connector at the mirror (headliner or door)

U0515.d: The remote function actuation module picks up the radio signals of key fobs and, on newer vehicles, of a phone used as a key, and hands lock, unlock, liftgate or remote start requests to the body controller. U0515 means its messages reach the network but fail the receiver's checks.
s: Key fob or phone-as-a-key not working or only intermittently
Passive entry or remote start unavailable
Network codes stored in several body modules at the same time
c: Module software hanging or outdated, e.g. after an over-the-air update
Chafed or pinched data wire to the receiver module in the roof area
Supply interruption or internal fault of the receiver module

U0516.d: Here a door switch is a networked switch pack in a door trim panel that reports window, lock or mirror requests as data instead of through separate wires. U0516 is stored when frames from switch unit A arrive but fail the receiver's validity checks.
s: Buttons on one door switch pack without function
Window or lock on that door only operable from other switches
c: Electronics of switch unit A faulty (moisture, cracked solder joints)
Damaged data or ground wire in the door harness
Replacement switch of the wrong variant or software level

U0517.d: Door switch B is the only letter of this series with a published manufacturer assignment. FCA bulletin 08-013-15 for the 2014 Jeep Cherokee (KL) gives the partner code U0216 as lost communication with the driver door switch; it showed up after the battery had been disconnected, together with a Start/Stop Not Available message, and was cured with new BCM software and a restored proxi configuration.
s: Driver's master window switches or window lockout not working
Lock or mirror adjustment from the driver's door unavailable
Start/Stop Not Available message (FCA, with partner code)
c: BCM software or vehicle configuration out of step after battery disconnection (FCA KL)
Driver door switch pack faulty, e.g. after liquid ingress
Chafed data or ground wire between body and driver door

U0518.d: U0518 is set when a receiving controller gets data from door switch unit C that it cannot trust. Which door that is remains unpublished, and no manufacturer documents the code.
s: Controls on one door respond only sometimes
Fault appears when the door is opened or closed
c: Partly broken data or ground wire in the door hinge area
Supply dips while motors start (weak battery, poor ground)

U0519.d: Door switch unit D reports the positions of its buttons as coded data. Inside such packs several contacts often share one input through resistor networks or comparators, as Microchip explains for the switch interface of its LIN chips ATA6641/ATA6642, and the stages of a window rocker are distinguished by voltage level.
s: Window moves the wrong way or not at all from this switch
Express function triggered or missing unexpectedly
c: Worn, sticky or wet contacts producing impossible switch combinations
Electronics of switch unit D faulty
Poor ground or damaged data wire to the switch

U051A.d: U051A concerns door switch unit E. On a car with four side doors, A to D would already be enough for one unit per door, so E suggests an additional switch location; no manufacturer documents this code or says what E means.
s: Switch at an additional door position without function
Window at that position operable only from the driver's door
c: Switch unit E internally faulty or water-damaged
Fault on the LIN sub-bus wiring between door controller and switch
Switch variant not matching the vehicle configuration

U0521.d: Door switch unit F lies beyond the usual four side doors. Vans and large SUVs may carry further switch panels, for example at sliding doors or for a third seat row, but no manufacturer states which position F denotes or documents this code.
s: Switch panel at a sliding door or rear row not working
Windows or locks served by that panel do not respond to it
c: Worn wiring or contacts at a sliding or rear door transition
Switch or controller software not matching after replacement

U0522.d: J2012 provides seven door switch units, and G is the last of them. Few vehicles need that many networked switch packs, and no manufacturer publishes what G stands for or documents U0522.
s: One additional switch panel ignored by the vehicle
Code appears after a switch or module replacement
c: Switch variant or body controller configuration not matching
Data or supply wire to switch unit G damaged

U0523.d: A door window motor in the J2012 sense is a lift motor with its own electronics that talks to the network, usually as a LIN slave of a door or body controller. Such a unit reports where the glass is, based on its Hall pulses, whether it stopped for an obstacle or a stall and whether its sensor or supply has failed, as NXP's MM908E624 reference design (AN3147) shows.
s: Window moves only while the switch is held
Express up/down or comfort closing unavailable
Window stops part way
c: Electronics or Hall sensor in window motor A faulty
Window position not learned after battery disconnection or repair
Damaged LIN, supply or ground wire to the motor

U0524.d: U0524 means the master accepts frames from window motor B but not what they say. A common reason is a position value the controller cannot reconcile.
s: One-touch operation lost on that window
Window stops short of the top or reverses near the seal
c: End positions lost after battery disconnection, motor or regulator work
Hall sensor in motor B faulty, giving erratic position counts
Regulator cable or glass clamp slipped, so travel no longer matches

U0525.d: Data from window motor C include what the door controller needs for automatic closing, which in the United States falls under FMVSS 118. A window able to close without the switch being held must stop and reverse before it presses on a test rod of 4 to 200 mm with 100 N or more, and then open again by at least 125 mm or far enough for a 200 mm rod.
s: Automatic closing on locking does not close this window
Window only operable with the switch held
c: Motor C electronics sending corrupted status
Voltage drop at the motor during start-up (weak battery, poor ground)
Chafed LIN wire in the door harness

U0526.d: Not every lift motor carries Hall sensors. Patent US11611297 describes a cheaper approach in which the controller derives speed, current and how quickly current changes from the ripple that commutation leaves in the motor current, and recognises a pinch from those values.
s: Window halts part way or misjudges its end position
Express and comfort closing unavailable
c: Position counting from current ripple disturbed (brush wear, supply noise)
Window motor D or its electronics faulty
Poor ground or connector at the door

U0527.d: U0527 is logged when a receiver rejects the content sent by window motor E. Mechanics can play a part.
s: Window reverses without an obstacle while closing
Glass closes slowly or stops before the seal
c: Glass binding in the run channel or sash, distorting motor load

U0528.d: Window motor F is one of the slots beyond the four usual side doors; it could serve, for instance, powered rear quarter glass or a sliding door window, but no manufacturer documents which window F stands for or publishes U0528. Such motors report through status signals: in NXP's LIN 2.0 window lift example (AN2960) the slave returns an error flag for its last action plus a LIN response-error bit, which lets the maste
s: An additional power window moves only partly or not at all
Code appears after a motor has been replaced
c: Replacement motor with a different variant or node configuration
Damaged wiring at a sliding door or rear body transition

U0529.d: With G, J2012 reaches the seventh and last window motor slot, more than most vehicles will ever use. No manufacturer publishes U0529 or names a window for G.
s: Window stops responding after several operations
Automatic functions of that window disabled
c: Weak supply or ground causing faults under starting current
Window motor G or its electronics faulty
Motor electronics overheated after repeated operation

U052A.d: The heated steering wheel module powers the heating mat in the rim and reports its state, such as heater on or off, the requested level and the rim temperature read by an embedded thermistor, to the body or climate network. A receiver that gets these frames but finds the content implausible (temperature out of range, bad checksum or counter, wrong length) logs U052A; if the frames stop entirely, U0229 is set instead.
s: Heated steering wheel stays cold or switches off early
Heater indicator or menu shows no or wrong status
c: Rim temperature sensor drifting or open, giving implausible values
Worn clock spring or steering wheel wiring to the heater circuit
Heated steering wheel module internally faulty
Module software or configuration not matching after programming

U052F.d: Object detection maintenance control modules appear in the generic code list, but no manufacturer has published what they do or when this fault sets. The name points to a unit that keeps cameras, radar or lidar used for object detection usable, for example by running washers, air jets or heaters.
s: Sensor blocked or sensor cleaning message
Driver assistance features temporarily unavailable
Sensor washing or heating not working
c: Software or configuration mismatch of maintenance module A
Internal fault of the maintenance module (e.g. moisture ingress)
Wiring or connector fault on the module's data line

U0530.d: Module B of this family is a second maintenance controller for object detection sensors, for instance one serving another sensor group or the other side of the vehicle. The generic definition offers no public explanation, and no manufacturer document names U0530.
s: Message that a sensor or assistance function is unavailable
Automatic sensor cleaning on one side or sensor group not working
c: Software level of module B not matching the receiving controller
Module B internal fault, e.g. after water or road salt exposure
Intermittent contact in the data line or connector to module B

U0531.d: The rear gate module runs a powered liftgate or tailgate: motor drive, latch, pinch sensing and the requests from switches or key fob. U0531 is stored when its messages reach other controllers with content they refuse.
s: Power liftgate does not open or close electrically
Liftgate reverses at the fully closed position
Interior lamps or other body functions fail at the same time (shared LAN)
c: Water ingress or corrosion in connectors at the liftgate
Liftgate module software fault (update available on some models)
Broken wires in the harness passing through the liftgate hinge area
Hinge or drive damage after repeated obstruction while closing

U0532.d: The rain sensing module behind the windshield measures how much infrared light wet glass scatters and, in most designs, also reads ambient light for automatic headlamps. Melexis describes such a unit as an optical front end, a microcontroller and a LIN system basis chip linking it to the body controller.
s: Automatic wipers do not react to rain or wipe on a dry screen
Automatic headlamps switch late, early or not at all
c: Rain and light sensor electronics faulty
Sensor badly coupled to the glass or wrong variant after windshield replacement
Corroded connector or chafed LIN wire at the windshield headliner
Body controller software evaluating the sensor frames incorrectly

U0533.d: Side obstacle detection modules are the corner radars behind the rear bumper that watch blind spots and crossing traffic. GM and Ford give letter A to the left unit: the 2011 Saab 9-5 code list names U0232 for the left side-object module, and Ford bulletin 24-2180 (Expedition/Navigator 2022-2024) logs U0232 in Ford's IPMA camera module together with faults of the left radar.
s: Blind spot monitoring unavailable message
Left mirror warning indicator inoperative
Rear cross traffic alert switched off
c: Mud, ice or damage at the left rear radar, bracket or bumper cover
Water or corrosion in the radar connector or harness
Radar module software or configuration fault

U0534.d: Module B is the right-hand rear corner radar in GM and Ford numbering: Saab's 2011 list calls U0233 the right side-object module, and Ford's Expedition/Navigator bulletin 24-2180 pairs U0233 with the right sensor. Toyota uses U0233 for the master sensor of the Tacoma blind spot system, where bulletin T-SB-0063-19 had both sensors replaced and re-aimed with a reflector tool.
s: Right mirror blind spot indicator not working
Cross traffic alert unavailable
Service message for the blind spot system
c: Moisture or corrosion at the right radar connector
Right radar damaged or misaligned after a bumper impact
Internal fault or outdated software in the right radar module

U0535.d: A convenience recall module keeps driver profiles and moves seat, mirrors, adjustable pedals or steering column back to stored positions, typically on a memory button or when the key fob linked to a profile unlocks the car. Ford's patent filing lists profiles covering seat, mirror, pedal and steering adjustment, and a Lear/Ford patent places a memory seat module with position sensors on the seat frame; Ram's owner's
s: Memory buttons or key-linked profiles do not restore positions
Seat or mirrors move to wrong positions or stop part-way
c: Seat, mirror or pedal position sensor reporting implausible values
Memory module internally faulty or stored profiles corrupted
Pinched or corroded wiring under the seat or in the door
Module not configured or positions not relearned after replacement

U0536.d: Lateral acceleration tells the stability system how hard the car is being pushed sideways in a bend; set against yaw rate and steering input it reveals whether the vehicle still follows the driver. U0536 is logged by a receiving module, usually the brake or ESC controller, when frames from a stand-alone lateral acceleration sensor module are present but unusable, for instance a reading beyond physical limits, an inva
s: ESC and traction control lamps lit
No stability or traction intervention when cornering
Hill hold or adaptive cruise may be unavailable
c: Acceleration sensor element faulty or out of calibration
Module mounted loosely or in the wrong orientation after repair work
Corrosion or moisture at the module connector (often under seats or console)
Software or coding mismatch between sensor module and receiver

U0537.d: The column lock module drives the electric bolt that blocks the steering shaft when the car is parked and frees it before the engine may start. U0537 records that a partner module, such as the body controller or keyless start unit, received lock status messages it cannot trust.
s: Engine does not start or start is refused
Steering wheel remains locked
Steering column lock service message
c: Column lock module software or calibration fault (reprogramming)
Weak 12 V battery or voltage drops during start
Lock module not paired/learned to the body or immobilizer module after replacement
Mechanical or internal fault of the lock actuator

U0538.d: Digital audio control modules are the networked parts of a sound system such as amplifiers, signal processors or media interfaces; the letters A to D merely count them. Ford groups U0237 and U0238, the lost-communication codes for modules C and D, with DSP trouble: 2020–2021 Escape, 2021 F-150, Mach-E, Expedition, Explorer and 2020–2022 Edge could lose all sound while chimes moved to the cluster, cured by a battery-d
s: No sound or missing speaker channels
Warning chimes only from the instrument cluster
c: Audio module software fault, as in Ford's DSP cases
Poor fuse contact or low supply voltage at the module

U0539.d: Ford assigns the D slot fairly clearly: on 2024–2026 Nautilus, 2025–2026 Aviator with the 28-speaker system and 2025–2026 Navigator, the audio control module stores U0238 when it cannot reach the digital signal processor (SSM 54751, 54752). The first check there is pulling the DSP fuse for one minute; only when contact returns are a fuse fault or a new DSP the answer, and on Nautilus and Navigator a software fix was
s: No audio from the speakers although the radio display works
Sound drops out intermittently or some channels are missing
c: Poor blade contact at the DSP fuse or supply interruption
DSP or audio control module software fault

U053A.d: Entrapment control modules handle pinch protection for powered closures where it is not built into the drive, typically sliding doors, liftgates or roofs with sensing edges. For windows, roof panels and partitions FMVSS 118 sets the goal: stop and reverse before 100 N act on the test rod.
s: Power closure will not close automatically
Closure reverses without an obstacle
c: Entrapment control module A internally faulty or with wrong software
Damaged pinch sensor edge feeding implausible values into the module
Bus wiring to the module damaged, e.g. in a liftgate or door hinge

U053B.d: Image processing modules evaluate camera data for assistance functions, and module A is the one most often named in service literature. GM's 2025 brake controller tables (25OBDG04A) check protection values and rolling counters in messages from the object fusion controller (EOCM); 3 errors in a window of 16 frames set U053B as Type C without MIL, and the test pauses outside 9 to 16 V.
s: Lane keeping or adaptive cruise unavailable message
Remote park assist or automatic hitch function refused
Code stored without noticeable symptoms
c: Software in image processing module A (update available, e.g. Ford Maverick)
Steering angle not relearned after battery disconnect or transport mode (Jeep Compass)
Front camera not calibrated after windshield or module replacement
Supply voltage outside the valid window during start-up

U053C.d: U053C is documented by GM on cars with Super Cruise. On the 2023 Cadillac Lyriq it could set at start-up and remain current for as long as half an hour, keeping Super Cruise unavailable; an ignition cycle cleared it in some cases only (PIC6500).
s: Super Cruise Unavailable message
Adaptive cruise or Service Driver Assist message
Surround view camera display faulty (other makes)
c: Software behaviour at start-up between the image processing modules (GM Super Cruise)
Stored history code unrelated to the actual fault (GM PIC6607)
Fault in module B or its network connection

U053D.d: No manufacturer text cites U053D. GM does show which unit occupies slot C: bulletin 21-NA-209 for the 2021 Escalade identifies U023C as the code for a silent K157 video processing module, where a software fault left the radio screen black with a crossed-out camera symbol until a fuse reset and reprogramming.
s: Black or missing camera image on the central display
Camera-based assistance functions unavailable
c: Software anomaly in the video/image processing module C
Module locked up, cleared by power reset (fuse) and reprogramming
Damaged video or network cable to module C

U0541.d: Entrapment control module B is the second slot for a separate pinch-protection unit. Some designs detect a person before contact: a capacitive strip changes its electric field as a hand approaches, and the attached electronics pass the result to the closure controller either as a switched output or as LIN or SAE J2602 data, as a review of tailgate anti-pinch approaches explains; patent US20030151382 likewise combines
s: Power liftgate or sliding door stops or reverses without contact
Automatic closing refused with a warning
c: Capacitive sensor strip or its electronics delivering implausible values
Sensor connector not fully seated or corroded
Software or calibration of module B not matching after replacement

U0542.d: Headlamp control modules run adaptive lighting such as swivelling, levelling, matrix segments and LED daytime lights, frequently with one module per headlamp. U0542 means a receiver, for example the body or lighting master module, gets messages from module A that fail its checks.
s: Check headlamp or lighting system warning
Adaptive or cornering light not working on one side
Daytime running light or position light affected
c: Headlamp or module replaced without coding/configuration
Moisture or corrosion at the headlamp connector

U0543.d: Headlamp control module B is the second light controller, usually serving the headlamp opposite module A. Bentley's 2019-2020 Continental GT campaign (2056293/1) handles the two as light control left and right, at diagnostic addresses 29 and 39, and both needed new software when the outer daytime running lights failed.
s: Lighting system warning in the cluster
Matrix or bending light on one side fixed to low beam
Daytime running light on one side out
c: Different or outdated software in headlamp module B compared with A
Internal fault in headlamp module B

U0544.d: Parking assist control modules evaluate the ultrasonic sensors in the bumpers and work out distances or steering paths. Mercedes-Benz lists U0544 in its Intelligent Predictive Repair guide for its eight-gear DCT (models 118, 177, 247; document LI27.00-P-077141): the transmission controller stores U054487 when data from the PARKTRONIC unit are implausible, and failure type 87 points to a missing message.
s: Parking sensors or park assist switched off with warning
Automatic parking manoeuvre not available
Transmission control unit stores the code (Mercedes DCT)
c: Internal or software fault in parking assist module B
Messages from module B missing or delayed (bus fault, module reset)
Damaged bumper harness or sensors causing module B to send invalid data

U0545.d: Power running boards deploy when a door opens and retract when it closes or the vehicle moves; a running board control module (Ford: RBM) drives the motors and reports position and faults. U0545 means its data reach other modules but are rejected.
s: Running boards do not deploy or retract, fault message in the cluster
Running board setting changes from Auto to Off by itself
c: Software fault in the running board or hosting seat module
Low battery voltage event corrupting module data
Implausible motor position feedback from dirt, ice or corrosion at the board

U0546.d: The front entertainment control module is the media unit for the front row, usually the head unit or a separate media controller that also supplies rear systems. Visteon's patent describes this layout: a main unit for the front seats and an entertainment module for rear passengers, each with its own microcontroller, trade commands and status as multiplex messages, with the front unit steering sources for the rear.
s: Rear entertainment loses its source or control from the front
Wrong or frozen media information on displays
c: Head unit or media controller software fault
Damaged media bus wiring or connector behind the dash

U0547.d: Seat control module E belongs to the higher letters used once a car has more seat electronics than a driver and a passenger unit. Ford uses the E slot for a climate seat controller on the 2016 Lincoln MKX, where weak seat cooling was fixed by updating the as-built configuration of the SCME (SSM 46279).
s: Seat heating or ventilation switches off or stays at one level
Seat climate setting on the screen does not match the seat
c: Wrong as-built configuration or software in the seat module
Seat temperature sensor or thermoelectric element giving implausible values
Loose or corroded connector under the seat

U0548.d: For seat control module F no manufacturer publishes an official assignment, and U0548 appears in no bulletin. Ford's naming shows how far seat letters reach: B for the front passenger, G and H for multi-contour units, J for third-row power folding and K/L for the second-row power seats of the 2025 Navigator (SSM 54226), so F is one more seat node, possibly in a rear row.
s: Functions of one particular seat unavailable
Seat switch or screen control for that seat does not react
c: Harness pinched in seat rails or folding mechanism
Module not configured to the vehicle after replacement

U0549.d: No manufacturer explains in public what the remote accessory module is; the term shows up only in code lists, together with its lost-communication partner U0248. Going by the name, it is a body-side unit controlling accessories away from the main controllers, and it is distinct from the accessory protocol interface module covered by U0554.
s: An accessory function controlled by this module does not work
Code stored without noticeable effect
c: Retrofitted or upfitter equipment disturbing the module's data
Low battery voltage or power interruption while the module was active

U054A.d: Some vehicles carry two rear entertainment units, for instance one screen per front headrest or separate units for second and third rows, which J2012 numbers Rear A and Rear B. GM's Saab 9-5 code list shows such a split: U0196 for the rear audio control module and U0249, the lost-communication partner of U054A, for a rear radio audio control module.
s: Second rear screen shows no picture or wrong source
Headphones or remote of that screen do not respond
c: Rear entertainment unit B internally faulty
Strained wiring through seat, headrest or headliner to unit B
Software level of unit B not matching the front unit

U054B.d: Interior lighting control module A runs cabin illumination such as dome, footwell and ambient light strips, in newer cars often RGB LED nodes on a LIN line below the body controller. Microchip's reference ambient lighting module shows the data involved: the master sends a command frame with zone, colour shares and intensity and asks for a status frame in return, each protected by a LIN checksum at 10.4 kbit/s.
s: Interior or ambient lights stay off or flicker
Ambient colour or brightness differs from the setting
c: LED driver node or lighting module internally faulty
Chafed LIN line or loose connector in trim or headliner
Wrong vehicle configuration for the lighting variant

U054C.d: Ford gives seat control module G a fixed meaning: SCMG is the driver's multi-contour seat module with massage and lumbar functions. Ford's TSB 19-2293 covers vehicles from the 2013 MKZ to the 2019 F-150 and Navigator with intermittent massage and lumbar operation, B1471 and U024B/U024C, caused by fretting terminals at the SCMG and SCMH connectors and fixed with new pigtails and a rerouted harness.
s: Driver seat massage or lumbar adjustment works only intermittently
Seat contour settings cannot be operated from the touchscreen
c: Fretting corrosion at the multi-contour seat module connector
Seat module misconfigured after a software update

U054D.d: Seat control module H is Ford's multi-contour module for the passenger seat (SCMH), the counterpart of SCMG. On 2022 Explorer and Aviator an intermittent passenger massage function without any stored code was traced to the configuration of both modules; first no fix was available, later reprogramming plus the configuration apps solved it (SSM 50591, 51927).
s: Passenger seat massage starts and stops on its own
Passenger lumbar or contour adjustment does not respond
c: Passenger seat module configuration not matching the vehicle
Fretting corrosion at the passenger seat module connector
Passenger multi-contour seat module internally faulty

U054E.d: Ford calls the module that folds the third-row seats electrically both PFSM and seat control module J (SCMJ). On 2025–2026 Expedition and Navigator its software left the seats unwilling to fold when 3L, Both or 3R was pressed, restored by a relearn in which Both is held for one minute and then five seconds more (SSM 53681), and caused misaligned upright seats after an obstruction reset (SSM 54613).
s: Third-row seats do not fold or unfold electrically
Seats stop part-way or end up misaligned
c: Power fold seat module software fault
Seat end positions lost after an obstruction event or power loss
Harness to the third-row seats damaged in the cargo area

U054F.d: Some vehicles carry more than two side obstacle radars, adding units for wider coverage of lane changes and crossing traffic. Ford names them side obstacle detection control modules C and D (SODCMC, SODCMD) next to the left and right units SODL and SODR.
s: Side assistance or blind spot warning message
Lane change or cross traffic warnings partly unavailable
c: Module C not configured or VIN not written after replacement
Software level of module C outdated or incompatible
Harness or connector fault at module C

U0550.d: Module D is the fourth radar of a side obstacle system, in Ford terms SODCMD alongside SODL, SODR and SODCMC. Which corner it serves depends on the vehicle and is not stated in the public Ford bulletins.
s: Side assistance or cross traffic alert switched off
Warning message about a blocked or faulty sensor
c: Radar D or its bracket damaged by a bumper impact
Water ingress or corrosion at the module D connector
Replacement module D without vehicle configuration

U0551.d: An impact classification system module helps the restraint system judge what kind of collision is under way, for example frontal, side or angled, and how severe it is, so that the right airbags and pretensioners fire at the right stage. U0551 means another module, typically the airbag or restraint controller, receives messages from this unit whose content fails its plausibility or integrity checks.
s: Airbag/SRS warning lamp on
Restraint system message in the instrument cluster
Passenger airbag status indicator behaving abnormally
c: Internal fault in the impact classification module
Module or restraint controller not configured/programmed after replacement or crash repair
Damaged wiring or connector after collision or interior work

U0552.d: A second running board controller only makes sense where each side of the vehicle has its own electronics. A 2004 Ford patent for powered boards has one central module drive the left and right boards separately, so a design with one node per side is plausible, but no manufacturer publishes which side B would be.
s: Running board on one side no longer deploys or retracts
Running board setting changes from Auto to Off without driver input
c: Battery undervoltage or discharged battery disturbing the running board electronics
Running board module software fault (Ford fixes comparable faults by reprogramming)
Corroded connector or chafed wiring at the board motor under the body
Running board control module B internally faulty

U0553.d: Rear lighting control module B is a second controller for the rear lamps. U0553 is set when its messages are received but their content is implausible.
s: Trailer lamps or trailer brake function reported as faulty
Individual rear lamps not working
Several warning messages after battery or ground work
c: Trailer or rear lighting module software hung or outdated (Ford remedy is reprogramming)
Loose or badly tightened ground connection
Corrosion or short at the trailer socket feeding back into the module
Rear lighting control module B internally faulty

U0554.d: Accessory protocol interface module is Ford's name for the SYNC computer (APIM), which, at least in the first SYNC generation, sits apart from the audio control module and talks to the high- and medium-speed CAN buses. Because the touchscreen sends drive mode, settings and configuration through it, wrong APIM data reach far: on the 2021–2023 Mustang Mach-E, APIM software let the drive mode fall back to normal with Dr
s: Drive mode or vehicle settings chosen on the touchscreen are not applied or fall back
Wrong or incomplete information on the center display
Code stored in another module without noticeable fault
c: Outdated or faulty SYNC/APIM software (often fixed by an over-the-air or dealer update)
APIM configuration not matching the vehicle equipment after replacement or update
Receiving module (e.g. ABS) evaluating APIM data with outdated software

U0555.d: A remote start module lets the engine run from a key fob or app for heating or cooling and must work around the immobilizer while doing so; it may be a factory part, a dealer accessory or an aftermarket box tied into the CAN network. GM lists the remote start module as its own node (Saab 9-5 2011: U0254).
s: Engine does not start or shuts down again when started remotely
Code found during an all-systems scan with no noticeable fault
Module programming at the workshop does not complete
c: Aftermarket remote starter or other add-on device on the CAN bus sending non-conforming messages
Software of the remote start module not matching the vehicle gateway
Poor splices or connectors from the remote starter installation

U0556.d: The front display interface module is the screen unit in the center of the dash; GM calls the matching node info display module (Saab 9-5 2011, U0255), Ford uses FDIM. The display mostly shows what other modules feed it.
s: Touchscreen does not respond or reacts to inputs that were not made
Wrong or incomplete content shown on the center display
c: Display module software fault or level not matching the infotainment unit
Wrong configuration of display or infotainment module after replacement or update
Front display module internally faulty (touch sensor or electronics)

U0557.d: Front controls interface module A is the button panel in the center stack that reads keys and knobs for audio and climate and passes them on as bus messages; Ford calls it FCIM, GM the infotainment faceplate control module (Saab 9-5 2011, U0256). Ford shows how much depends on it: on 2015–2017 F-150 trucks heavy CAN traffic could freeze the FCIM, so A/C, radio and even window switch control failed intermittently with
s: Radio or climate buttons work only intermittently or not at all
Several warning lamps or messages appear together with the button failure
c: Control panel electronics locking up under high bus load
Control panel software fault or mismatch with the infotainment unit
Stuck button or liquid spilled into the panel producing invalid key states
Front controls interface module A internally faulty

U0558.d: Simpler infotainment systems put buttons and a small screen into one unit, the front controls/display interface module. Ford calls it FCDIM, used for example with the 4-inch audio display, and the GM-built 2011 Saab 9-5 lists U0257 for its info display module/infotainment faceplate control module.
s: Radio presets cannot be stored or recalled, preset keys act erratically
Small audio display blank or showing wrong settings
c: Software fault in the combined controls/display unit (Ford remedy is reprogramming)
Unit programmed with a calibration for a different equipment level
Front controls/display interface module internally faulty

U0559.d: Despite the name, the radio transceiver is not the audio tuner but the module that exchanges radio signals with keys and wireless accessories. Ford's name is RTM: on 2021–2022 Bronco Sport, jammed passive-key frequencies or a weak key battery could trigger No Key Detected, solved by placing the key in the console backup spot close to the RTM (SSM 50341); on recent F-150 and Super Duty trucks the RTM uses a new freque
s: No Key Detected or similar key message in the cluster
Keyless entry or remote functions work poorly or not at all
Wireless keypad cannot be paired
c: Radio interference or weak key battery producing implausible receiver data
Accessory keypad or remote on a frequency the transceiver does not support

U055A.d: Special purpose vehicle control modules are add-on controllers that body builders and upfitters fit to police cars, ambulances, utility trucks and similar conversions. U055A means frames from module A arrive but their content fails the receiver's checks.
s: Upfitter equipment (lights, outputs, interlocks) works erratically or not at all
Code stored without warning lamp
c: Upfitter module programmed or configured for a different vehicle software level
Vehicle modules updated without matching the upfitter module
Poorly made bus connection or splice in the body builder's wiring
Special purpose module A internally faulty

U055B.d: U055B concerns the second slot reserved for special purpose controllers. A receiving module gets frames from controller B, but a signal lies outside its permitted span, a counter or checksum is wrong, or the frame length does not match.
s: One group of conversion functions fails while others still work
Fault entry in the receiving module, usually without warning lamp
c: Second add-on controller set up with wrong address or message set
Software of add-on controller B and vehicle modules not matched
Unstable supply or ground at controller B, e.g. on a shared accessory feed

U055C.d: With U055C a module rejects the content of messages sent by special purpose controller C, the third of four slots for conversion electronics. No maker publishes a code-specific description.
s: Functions controlled by the conversion do not respond as configured
Code appears after a software update or conversion work
c: Software levels of conversion controller and vehicle modules out of step
Conversion equipment added or changed without updating controller C
Damaged bus wiring in the conversion harness

U055D.d: U055D is the last of the four special purpose controller codes. It is stored when frames from controller D reach the network but carry values the receiver rejects.
s: Individual conversion functions fail intermittently
Fault entry without effect on engine or brakes
c: Incomplete or interrupted software update of controller D
Voltage dip from heavy conversion loads corrupting controller D's output

U055E.d: Where the front switches are split over two panels, the second one is front controls interface module B. Ford uses exactly this name (FCIMB): on 2023 Transit vans with SYNC 3 Lite, rear-only parking aid and no front sensors, the parking aid disable switch sits in the FCIMB; for vehicles built between mid-March and early June 2023 it did nothing because the park aid module was misconfigured, fixed with the PAM configu
s: Switches on the second front panel have no effect
Indicator lamps in the switches do not match the actual function state
c: Receiving module configured for different equipment and misreading the panel B data
Software fault in the second control panel
Loose connector or damaged wiring behind the second panel

U055F.d: An electronic brake booster replaces the vacuum servo: a travel sensor reads the pedal and an electric motor supplies the assist, as in Bosch's iBooster, which also lets the brake system blend in regenerative braking and back up the stability control unit. U055F is set when booster A transmits but its data, such as pedal travel, assist status or pressure request, fail the receiver's checks.
s: ABS, brake or stability warning lamps on
Harder pedal or changed pedal feel
Regenerative braking or driver assistance functions limited
c: Booster control unit or its pedal travel sensor faulty
Supply interrupted or weak battery during start or service work
Booster and ABS/ESC software not matched
Bus wiring or connector at the booster damaged

U0560.d: A second brake booster unit mainly appears in architectures built for automated driving, where a single electronic brake must not be a single point of failure. Bosch, for example, pairs its integrated power brake with a separate redundant brake unit that can stop the car if the primary unit fails.
s: Brake system warning lamp or message on
Driver assistance or automated functions unavailable
c: Secondary brake unit B internally faulty
Software of the two brake units not matched after update or replacement
Separate supply or ground of unit B faulty

U0561.d: Modern power seat switches are often small control units of their own: they read the keys and send the result to the seat module over LIN instead of switching motor current directly. A Lear patent describes a seat electronics unit with a LIN driver that acts on commands from such an external switch.
s: Seat cannot be adjusted with the switch
Seat settings such as lumbar not shown or not selectable on the screen
c: Seat switch module software fault (e.g. switch stays in sleep mode)
Switch part or software level not matching the seat module
Loose or corroded connector at the seat or door switch
Seat control switch module A internally faulty

U0562.d: Switch module B is a second, separate seat switch unit, for the passenger side or another seat row; which position B denotes is not published by any manufacturer. Mercedes counts its seat switch groups by position, front left being SSE-VL, which points to one unit per seat.
s: Passenger or rear seat does not move when its switch is pressed
Seat moves only in some directions
c: Receiving seat module not configured for the installed switch and seat equipment
Software fault in the second seat switch module
Connector or harness under a movable seat damaged by seat travel or objects

U0563.d: Premium sound systems often use an external amplifier away from the head unit, and large installations can need a second one, audio amplifier B. Such amplifiers are network nodes: the head unit sends volume and other commands over CAN instead of an analog level, and the amplifier reports its status back, as a patent on modular vehicle amplifiers explains.
s: Some speakers or the subwoofer silent while others play
Volume or sound settings react incorrectly
c: Amplifier B software not matching the head unit software level
Aftermarket amplifier or audio interface on the vehicle bus sending non-conforming data
Audio amplifier B internally faulty or overheated

U0564.d: In-car voice control lets the driver place calls, pick stations or play music by spoken command, in newer systems even in natural sentences. Some makers house it in a module of its own: FCA put Uconnect voice recognition into a hands-free module (HFM) on 2012–2017 Journey, Charger and 300; with old software it could hang while loading, ignore the steering-wheel voice key or pick up background noise, and a reflash fix
s: Voice control does not respond to the steering-wheel button
Voice commands misrecognized or system stuck while loading
c: Speech recognition software outdated or faulty (fixed by reflashing)
Unsupported language selection or mismatch between module and head unit settings

U0565.d: The rear camera module delivers the reversing picture and, on some vehicles, data that other controllers reuse. U0565 is logged by a receiver that gets its frames but judges the content implausible.
s: Hands-free driving or lane centering unavailable (Ford BlueCruise vehicles)
Reversing picture missing, frozen or without guide lines
Code stored in radio or driver-assist module without noticeable fault
c: Rear camera module software level not matching the receiving module (Ford remedy is reprogramming)
Receiver flags the camera data too strictly although the picture is fine (Jeep Gladiator 2024 radio)
Water or corrosion in the camera plug or tailgate harness

U0566.d: At GM, image processing sensor A is the front camera behind the windshield; its partner U0265 is called Front View Camera – Windshield in GM bulletins. GM's 2025 OBD tables show how U0566 is detected: the brake module and the EOCM3 driver-assist controller check rolling counters, checksums and message authentication on the camera's frames.
s: Service Driver Assist or Steering Assist Reduced message
Adaptive cruise and automatic braking functions unavailable
MIL possible only through accompanying brake-module code P25A2
c: Windshield camera software resets or sends faulty protection values (GM remedy is reprogramming)
Front camera internally faulty when the fault recurs often (GM then replaces it)
Supply voltage dips or bus disturbances during start

U0567.d: Image processing sensors are cameras that interpret their own picture and send results, not raw video, onto the bus. U0567 is set when frames from sensor B arrive but fail the receiver's checks, for instance a wrong CRC or a counter that jumps or repeats.
s: Assistance or night-view function served by sensor B switched off
Camera-related service message in the instrument cluster
c: Sensor B software not matching the receiver after an update or replacement
Loose connector or damaged wiring causing corrupted frames
Image processing sensor B internally faulty

U0568.d: U0568 means a receiver gets messages from image processing sensor C whose content it cannot trust. SAE only numbers these sensors; no manufacturer publishes which physical camera is C, and the partner U0267 appears in no public bulletin either.
s: Lane departure warning or traffic sign display unavailable
Automatic high beam falls back to manual switching with a warning
c: Software mismatch between sensor C and the receiving controller
Intermittent contact in the sensor connector or bus wiring
Image processing sensor C internally faulty

U0569.d: Sensor D's frames reach the receiver, but their content fails its plausibility or protection checks. Which camera carries letter D is not published, and U0569 itself appears in no bulletin.
s: Surround-view, park-assist or adaptive-cruise service messages
Front park, turn, daytime or cornering lamps out at the same time
Several camera and radar codes stored together
c: Front fascia or bumper harness chafed through (GM Escalade 2015–2020 pattern)
Blown fuse leaving the sensor with unstable supply
Image processing sensor D internally faulty or damaged in a collision

U056A.d: U056A is the invalid-data code for image processing sensor E: the module still talks, but the receiver rejects what it says. No brand documents U056A itself.
s: Object detection or Service Active Safety message
Scan tool cannot reach radars and front camera
Code returns only when one particular tester is connected
c: Faulty diagnostic interface or cable on the object detection bus pins (false codes)
Fault on the dedicated object detection bus wiring
Sensor E software fault or internal defect

U056B.d: At GM, the partner of U056B – U026A – belongs to the front camera module B174W. A 2023 GM note for 2022–2023 Cadillac XT5 and XT6, Chevrolet Equinox and GMC Acadia and Terrain blames U026A plus the front-camera warning on terminals in that camera that were pushed back or absent, which then has to be replaced.
s: Service Front Camera message
Lane keeping, lane departure or forward collision alert unavailable
c: Pushed-in or missing terminals in the front camera connector (GM 2022–2023)
Front camera software fault, fixed by reprogramming

U056C.d: Image processing sensor G is sending frames that the receiving module refuses. Neither U056C nor a camera position for G is documented by a manufacturer.
s: Surround view shows a black segment or is unavailable
Blown fuses and front lamps out at the same time
c: Bumper or fascia harness rubbed through, shorting circuits and fuses
Camera connector disturbed or misassembled after body repair
Image processing sensor G internally faulty

U056D.d: U056D is reported when sensor H's messages carry data that fail checks such as a CRC, an alive counter or an authentication value. AUTOSAR's end-to-end protection names the fault types behind this: repeated, lost, delayed, corrupted or masqueraded frames.
s: Single assistance function unavailable while others work
U056D stored without bus-off or other lost-communication codes
c: Sensor H software computing counters or checksums incorrectly
Poor contact at sensor H connector while the rest of the bus is fine
Image processing sensor H internally faulty

U056E.d: The higher letters of the image-sensor series cover the further cameras that newer vehicles add. One growing group looks into the cabin: driver monitoring cameras check whether the driver is watching the road, as Super Cruise does at Cadillac, starting with the 2017 CT6, or Ford's BlueCruise, which uses a module on the steering column of the 2021 Mustang Mach-E and F-150; in the EU such warning systems fall under reg
s: Hands-free or attention-dependent assistance not offered
Driver attention warning inactive or showing a fault
c: Sensor I software level not matching the receiving controller
Connector disturbed behind trim, dash or steering column panels
Image processing sensor I internally faulty

U056F.d: U056F concerns image processing sensor J, whose messages arrive but are not plausible. No manufacturer publishes this code, its partner U026E, or which camera carries the letter J.
s: Camera view black, frozen or replaced by a warning
Camera-related message in the instrument cluster
c: Software mismatch after an update of camera or display unit
Damaged wiring or connector at an exposed camera position (mirror housing, door)
Image processing sensor J internally faulty

U0570.d: Sensor K's frames reach the bus but are discarded as invalid. U0570 and its partner U026F are not documented by any vehicle maker, so the camera behind letter K is unknown.
s: Extra camera view (for example trailer view) missing or black
Code appears mainly with a trailer or accessory connected
c: Corroded or loose plug where an add-on or trailer camera connects
Additional camera not configured or software not matching the vehicle
Image processing sensor K internally faulty

U0571.d: U0571 closes the image-processing-sensor block; the next number, U0572, already belongs to a vehicle motion control module. An image processing sensor computes objects inside the camera itself, for instance with a system-on-chip as in Bosch's multi purpose camera or with Mobileye's EyeQ processors, the first generation of which launched in 2008.
s: Assistance function using sensor L unavailable
Code stored without warning lamp
c: Processing software in sensor L faulty or not matching the receiver
Wiring or connector fault corrupting the sensor's messages
Image processing sensor L internally faulty

U0572.d: A vehicle motion control module sits above the individual chassis controllers and coordinates steering, brakes, damping and drive torque. ZF's cubiX software works this way and went into production in the Lotus Eletre; Hitachi Astemo describes a central controller that sends time-referenced instructions to several actuator modules.
s: Chassis or stability warning message
Rear-axle steering, active roll control or drive modes switched off
Car drives with basic stability control only
c: Software of motion control module and chassis controllers not matched
Motion control module A internally faulty
Implausible sensor input to the module (yaw, steering angle) leading to invalid outputs

U0573.d: U0573 is the B variant: invalid data from a second vehicle motion control module. A second unit makes sense where coordination tasks are split, for example lateral and longitudinal motion, or where a backup must take over for automated driving.
s: Warning about reduced chassis or assistance functions
Automated or semi-automated driving functions unavailable
c: Lost time synchronisation between module B and the actuator controllers
Modules A and B on different software levels
Motion control module B internally faulty

U0574.d: Lighting driver control modules switch and dim individual LEDs or LED segments in modern headlamps. Lincoln's 2025 Navigator has four of them, labelled A to D, and an over-the-air release (25.10.08) for all four adjusted headlamp colour and brightness at start-up; NHTSA's summary adds an intermittent resistance fault that dropped the lamps to their lowest setting.
s: Adaptive or glare-free high beam unavailable
Headlamp colour or brightness wrong, lamps at reduced level
c: Lighting driver module software needing an update (Lincoln remedy over the air)
Moisture or poor contact at the headlamp connector
Lighting driver control module A internally faulty (often only with the headlamp)

U0575.d: U0575 flags implausible data from lighting driver control module B. Matrix headlamps split the high beam into many LEDs that a control unit switches individually; Audi introduced the first such glare-free system on the 2013 A8 with 25 segments per lamp.
s: Glare-free high beam switched off with a lighting message
Individual LED segments dark or flickering
c: Software of driver module B outdated or inconsistent with the other modules
Defective LED segment producing fault reports the receiver cannot match
Lighting driver control module B internally faulty

U0576.d: Lighting driver control module C is sending data that the receiver discards. The US standard FMVSS 108 explains why this matters for an adaptive driving beam: the system must recognise malfunctions, including a blocked sensor, switch to manual beam control until the fault is gone and show the driver a warning.
s: Lighting system warning in the instrument cluster
Automatic high beam replaced by manual switching
c: Driver module C software fault, curable by an update
Unstable supply or ground at the headlamp
Lighting driver control module C internally faulty

U0577.d: U0577 is the code for invalid messages from lighting driver control module D, the last of the four-letter block; U0276 is its lost-communication partner. LED matrix drivers can be chained: TI's TPS92662 addresses up to 31 devices over one multi-drop UART line, can use CAN transceivers for a sturdier physical layer, and also drives sequential turn signals and animated daytime lights.
s: Sequential indicator or animated daytime light not working
Lamp lit only in a basic setting
c: Driver module D software not at the level of the other lighting modules
Fault on the serial link between lighting controller and driver chips
Lighting driver control module D internally faulty

U0578.d: Ford assigns letter K to a defined seat: on the 2025 Lincoln Navigator, seat control module K (SCMK) is the rear left power seat module of the second row. Its software update SCMK-25.5.5.3 removed a short delay in seat operation and made the memory function of that seat store positions reliably.
s: Left second-row power seat responds late or does not move fore and aft
Memory positions of that seat not saved
c: Seat module K software fault (Ford remedy is a software update)
Seat module K not configured for the installed second-row seat equipment
Connector under the second-row seat loose or damaged

U0579.d: Seat control module L (SCML) is Ford's right-hand counterpart to SCMK: on the 2025 Lincoln Navigator it runs the passenger-side power seat of the second row. Ford pushed SCML-25.5.5.3 over the air so that this seat keeps its memory settings consistently; the release note page itself is headed with the PCM by mistake but names seat control module L in the text.
s: Right second-row power seat does not move with its switch
Stored seat positions on the passenger side lost
c: Seat module L software fault (fixed by an over-the-air update)
Seat module L configuration missing or wrong for the seat equipment

U057B.d: Charger C is the third on-board charger slot. Some vehicles split AC charging over several units: the extended-range Ford F-150 Lightning, for example, offers 19.2 kW through a dual on-board charger.
s: AC charging slower than expected
Charging fault message in the display or app
c: Charger C on a different software level than master or charging controller
Communication line between the chargers damaged

U057C.d: U057C covers the fourth charger slot. Large chargers are often built from parallel power modules: Hyundai's patent for a vehicle-mounted charger gives each module its own slave controller that reports to a master, which can drop to a single module once the battery reaches the constant-voltage phase.
s: Charging power lower than usual or charging stops
Charging system warning
c: Power module or slave controller D faulty
Charger software not matched across units
Overheating of unit D due to coolant or fan problems, corrupting its status data

U057D.d: Despite its name, the off-board charger control module sits inside the vehicle: it conducts the dialogue with an external DC fast charger, which under CCS runs as power line communication on the control pilot contact (ISO 15118, DIN 70121) and under CHAdeMO over a CAN link in the connector. Ford calls this unit the off-board charger controller (OBCC) on the Mustang Mach-E and E-Transit; SSM 50923 had new OBCC softwar
s: DC fast charging aborts or does not start
Charging works at other stations
c: Fault or outdated software in the charging station
Dirty or damaged communication contacts in plug or inlet
Vehicle charging controller software not compatible with the station

U0580.d: A haptic control module produces vibrations the driver feels, in the steering wheel, seat or a touch surface, mainly as a warning. Hyundai and Genesis use a separate haptic steering controller: on the 2015–2016 Genesis and 2017–2018 G80, B247100 for a vibration motor fault brought on the warning lamp and the controller was replaced (19-BE-001, 19-BE-001-G).
s: Steering wheel or seat no longer vibrates during lane or other warnings
Haptic system warning lamp or message in the cluster
c: Poor contact in the vibration motor circuit making the module report implausible status
Haptic controller internally faulty or on an old software level
Alert type setting (chime or vibration) not matching between modules

U0585.d: Active grille shutters close the front opening to cut drag and speed warm-up; CARB counts them as an off-cycle CO2 technology. The shutter actuator is usually a LIN slave of the engine controller.
s: Check engine light on
Shutters stay in a fixed position
Slightly higher fuel consumption
c: Shutter actuator A with faulty firmware or internal fault (GM PIT6133)
LIN wiring or connector at the front end damaged or wet
Replacement actuator of the wrong variant

U0586.d: Vehicles with two shutter assemblies, typically one in the upper grille and one in the lower bumper opening, report the second one as module B. U0586 means the engine controller gets status frames from that actuator but cannot trust them.
s: Check engine light on
Lower shutter does not move
c: Lower shutter actuator B with faulty firmware or internal fault
Wiring or connector in the lower bumper area damaged by road debris or water
Upper and lower actuator swapped or wrong part fitted

U0587.d: Some low-emission vehicles have a radiator coated with a catalyst that converts ground-level ozone, known as direct ozone reduction (DOR) or by BASF's trade name PremAir; it earns an emissions credit, and CARB then requires the OBD system to monitor it. A Ford patent filed by Swedish inventors describes the matching sensor: it is pressed into the radiator fins, reports radiator temperature, since the coating works ab
s: Check engine light on
No noticeable change in driving or cooling
c: Radiator replaced with an uncoated part or sensor moved from another radiator
Corroded connector or wiring at the radiator

U0588.d: An electric transmission fluid pump keeps clutch and line pressure up while the engine is stopped by start-stop or in electric hybrid driving. Many such pumps have their own electronics and report speed, current and faults to the transmission or hybrid controller.
s: Start-stop function disabled
Service transmission or hybrid system message
Limp mode with limited gears on some hybrids
c: Electric pump or its integrated controller faulty
Pump connector not fully latched or wet
Pump and transmission controller software not matched

U0589.d: A DC/AC converter turns the vehicle's DC supply into household-style AC for power outlets in the cabin or truck bed. Ford calls the 7.2 kW Pro Power Onboard unit of the 2021 F-150 PowerBoost direct current/alternating converter module A (DCACA) and fixed a service message there by reprogramming the PCM and the DCACA.
s: Power outlets dead or switching off under load
Message that the onboard power system needs service
c: Converter or receiving module software out of date (Ford DCACA reprogramming)
Body control module configured for an outlet option the vehicle does or does not have

U058A.d: U058A refers to a second DC/AC converter. Two converters can make sense when outlets in the cab and in the cargo bed are fed separately or when a high-power unit is added to a small one.
s: One group of outlets dead while others work
Outlet warning or service message
c: Configuration not updated after fitting or retrofitting converter B
Converter B internally faulty or overheated
Bus wiring to converter B damaged

U058B.d: Some transmissions carry a second electrically driven oil pump with its own electronics, labelled module B, alongside or instead of a first one. Its job is to hold clutch pressure and lubrication while the combustion engine is off, so the receiving transmission or hybrid controller depends on the speed, current and fault status the pump reports.
s: Start-stop or electric drive mode unavailable
Transmission warning message
Delayed engagement after an engine restart
c: Integrated electronics of electric pump B faulty
Pump B connector or pass-through in the transmission case wet or loose
Pump firmware and transmission controller software not compatible

U058C.d: A third grille shutter unit appears on vehicles that split the lower intake into several flaps. Hyundai is the clearest case: on the 2026 Palisade and Palisade Hybrid, the lower active air flaps use left and right actuators, and campaign 26-01-026H lists U028B, lost communication with shutter module C, among codes that light the engine lamp after water entered bumper connectors and corroded them.
s: Check engine light on
Active air flap warning message
Lower flaps stay in one position
c: Water ingress and corrosion at the lower bumper connectors (Hyundai 26-01-026H)
Shutter actuator C with internal electronics fault
Actuator of wrong variant or position fitted after a bumper repair

U058D.d: Module D is the fourth shutter position the code list reserves; it only matters on front ends with four separately driven flap sets, for instance two upper and two lower ones. No manufacturer documents U058D or names a shutter D in public material, so its exact placement remains maker-specific.
s: Check engine light on some vehicles
One flap set does not move
c: Shutter D wiring or LIN connector damaged by road debris or moisture
Engine controller configured for a shutter layout that does not match the vehicle

U0592.d: Shift-by-wire cars turn the driver's lever, dial or buttons into network messages; where two such units exist, or the selector is split from a park-lock unit, the second one is module B. U0592 says its messages arrive but carry an implausible selector position, a frozen counter or a bad checksum, so the receiver cannot rely on the requested gear.
s: Vehicle will not shift out of Park
Transmission fault message in the cluster
Restricted gear selection
c: Selector module B electronics or position sensing faulty
Bus wiring or gateway path between selector and transmission controller disturbed
Software of selector, gateway or TCM out of date

U0593.d: Electric vehicles with one motor per axle typically report the second inverter and motor as drive motor module B; on the 2019 Audi e-tron that is the rear unit, whose loss Audi logs as U0292 when a chafed low-voltage harness cuts it off. U0593 is set when that module keeps transmitting but its torque or status data are untrustworthy.
s: Drive system warning, reduced power
Reduced or no regenerative braking
Vehicle drives on one axle only
c: Low-voltage harness to the second drive unit chafed or connector loose
Drive motor B inverter or receiver software out of date

U0594.d: The hybrid or EV powertrain controller coordinates engine, motors and battery, so many modules read its messages. Ford's hybrid OBD summary explains that the ABS module logs U0594 when wheel-torque or driver-demand signals from the HPCM are flagged invalid, unknown or faulted; Ford's 2014 list carries it with MIL and its 2024 summary sets U0594_48 for bad monitoring data with MIL and wrench lamp.
s: Check engine light and hybrid or electrical system warning
Reduced power or stalling on some hybrids
Stored code without symptoms (Ford Escape, F-150 Lightning)
c: Fault inside the hybrid system makes the controller mark its signals invalid (e.g. MGU connector on Ram eTorque)
Software of the hybrid controller or the receiving module out of date

U0595.d: A powertrain control monitor module is an independent supervisor that recomputes torque, engine speed or pedal requests and compares them with what the main controller commands, so that unintended acceleration or deceleration can be caught. U0595 is stored when that supervisor's results arrive but cannot be trusted.
s: Wrench or powertrain warning lamp on
Reduced power or limp mode
c: Software mismatch between monitor module and main powertrain controller
Supply voltage dips or bus disturbances corrupting messages

U0596.d: An AC/AC converter changes alternating current of one voltage or frequency into another without handing it to the battery first. In vehicles, such a stage can sit in a charger, for example a matrix converter that turns three-phase grid power directly into high-frequency AC for an isolating transformer, as in patent US9973107B2, or it can adapt power for on-board outlets.
s: Charging or outlet power interrupted
Warning about the charging or power system
c: Converter control electronics faulty or overheated
Converter and receiving module software not matched
Bus wiring to the converter damaged

U0597.d: In plug-in hybrids and electric cars the AC/DC converter is normally the on-board charger: it rectifies mains power and controls the current into the traction battery. CARB requires plug-in hybrids to detect charger faults that stop charging or reduce its rate.
s: AC charging stops or runs at reduced rate
Electric-only mode unavailable on plug-in hybrids
Warning lamps such as ESC or check engine
c: Third-party dongle or Y-splitter on the diagnostic connector disturbing the bus (Volvo TJ 36559)
On-board charger electronics faulty or overheated
Charger or battery controller software out of date

U0598.d: A second AC/DC converter exists where makers raise AC charging power by fitting two charger units; the F-150 Lightning, for instance, can be ordered with two 40-amp charger units that together reach 19.2 kW. Patents show how the pair is run: Porsche's US10029578B2 has one charger lead and the other follow via a communication line only, and Hyundai's US10270273B2 uses a master controller with slave controllers per pow
s: AC charging only at roughly half power
Charging system warning
c: Second charger unit faulty or overheated
Software of the charger pair not matched after a replacement
Communication line between the chargers damaged

U0599.d: On start-stop vehicles a DC/DC converter can hold the 12 V supply for sensitive electronics while the starter pulls the voltage down; on hybrids it feeds the 12 V network from the high-voltage battery. GM's 2025 engine tables check the converter's output voltage and crank-control messages for alive counter, protection value and checksum errors and set U0599, Type B, after 8 failures in 18 samples with at least 11 V f
s: Auto start/stop disabled
Check engine light after repeated failures
c: Engine controller software miscalculating the converter's protection value (GM 20-NA-191)
Weak 12 V battery causing deep voltage dips during cranking

U059A.d: Converter B is a second DC/DC unit, used when one voltage support stage is not enough or when separate networks need their own supply. FCA is the only maker that names it publicly: in powertrain module updates for the 2019 Jeep Cherokee with the 3.2-litre V6 and engine stop-start (18-023-19 and follow-ups such as 18-020-21), the PCM lists both U0599 and U059A for invalid data from DC-to-DC converters A and B, plus U0
s: Check engine light
Engine does not restart after a stop-start event
Stop-start function withdrawn
c: Powertrain controller software evaluating converter B data incorrectly (FCA 18-023-19)
Wiring or ground connection of converter B poor

U059B.d: The battery pack sensor module measures pack voltage and current and often sits in the switch box that holds the main contactors, reporting to the battery management controller. Audi uses U059B00 for an implausible signal from the high-voltage battery switch box on the 2024 Q8 e-tron family: after a stop at an AC charging point the car refused to enable its drive and the cluster asked the driver to stop safely, with
s: Drive system cannot be activated
Drive system and electrical system fault messages
Charging interrupted
c: Current or voltage sensing in the switch box faulty
Battery-internal communication line or connector disturbed

U059C.d: A third drive motor controller exists only on tri-motor or quad-motor vehicles, where one axle carries two motors for torque vectoring. Examples are GMC's Hummer EV in tri-motor form and Rivian's quad-motor R1T with a motor at each wheel.
s: Propulsion system warning and reduced power
Torque vectoring or a drive mode unavailable
c: Inverter or controller of motor C faulty
Low-voltage harness or connector at drive unit C damaged
