Software level of motor C not matching the vehicle controller

U059D.d: Module D only exists where four drive motors are fitted, one per wheel. Rivian's R1T and R1S Quad-Motor are production examples: each wheel has its own motor, so a single faulty controller costs one corner of drive, not a whole axle.
s: Reduced power warning
Off-road or performance modes locked
c: Inverter or controller of the fourth motor faulty
Signal wiring at the wheel motor damaged by road debris or water
Motor controller software not updated together with the others

U059E.d: NOx sensor A usually sits upstream of the SCR catalyst. Its attached electronics turn the probe current into NOx and oxygen readings and broadcast them on CAN.
s: Check engine light after the second faulty trip
SCR and NOx sensor monitors stay incomplete
Engine usually runs normally
c: Sensor control unit of NOx sensor A faulty (heat, moisture, internal error)
Replacement sensor of a different part number or software level
Corroded connector or damaged CAN/supply wiring at the sensor
Engine controller software needing an update

U059F.d: Sensor B is normally the tailpipe NOx sensor behind the SCR catalyst, so its readings decide whether the catalyst efficiency test passes. The code means its CAN frames are present but unusable.
s: Check engine light on
SCR efficiency monitor not completing
No noticeable change in power
c: Engine controller calibration known to flag false faults (FCA reflash)
Control unit of the downstream NOx sensor damaged
Chafed wiring or water in the connector near the exhaust

U05A0.d: Some fuel systems hand the tank leak test to a separate module with its own pump, valve, pressure sensor and processor. Stoneridge patent US11773809 describes such a unit: it wakes hours after shutdown while the engine controller sleeps, runs the test alone and later passes pressure results over CAN or LIN, from which the OBD system decides on a fault code.
s: Check engine light on
EVAP readiness not set, emissions inspection may fail
c: Leak detection module electronics or its pressure sensor failing
Corrosion at the module connector near the tank or canister
Module and engine controller software levels do not match

U05A1.d: Here the fault is judged inside NOx sensor A: its control unit relies on engine controller frames, for instance the release to heat the probe once condensation is no longer a risk, and it reports back when those inputs are missing or make no sense. Ford's 2023 diesel OBD summary groups U05A1 with P2200 under the upstream NOx module checks.
s: Check engine light on
NOx reading for sensor A stays invalid on the scan tool
SCR monitors not completing
c: Engine controller software or configuration sending wrong values to the sensor
Intermittent CAN connection to the sensor causing timeouts
Sensor control unit misjudging correct data

U05A2.d: This is the downstream counterpart of U05A1: the tailpipe NOx sensor B finds the frames it gets from the engine controller missing or implausible and reports it. Ford's 2023 diesel summary documents it for the 3.0 L and 6.7 L engines next to P229E in the tailpipe NOx controller checks, using the same criteria as for the front sensor, an erroneous signal such as a dew point release with ignition off, or more than 1 s
s: Check engine light on
SCR efficiency monitor incomplete
c: Damaged harness to the rear sensor, exposed to road spray and heat
Engine controller software sending implausible commands
Fault inside the sensor B control unit

U05A3.d: A reductant quality module checks that the tank holds proper diesel exhaust fluid, a 32.5 % urea solution. SSI's TULC sensor, for example, derives concentration from the speed of sound and reports it with level and temperature over J1939 CAN to the dosing control unit.
s: Check engine light and DEF warning
Reductant consumption faults stored alongside
Possible speed or restart limitation if not fixed
c: Dosing control unit software misreading the module (FCA reflash)
Quality sensor fouled by crystals or contaminated fluid
Corroded connector at the DEF tank sender

U05A4.d: A diesel particulate matter sensor has its own control unit, which needs engine controller data to run its measuring and burn-off cycles. U05A4 is reported when that unit cannot accept what the engine controller sends.
s: Check engine light on
Several particulate matter sensor codes stored at once
Particulate filter monitor not completing
c: Engine controller software issue (FCA PCM update)
Damaged CAN or supply wiring to the PM sensor unit
PM sensor control unit faulty or wrong variant

U05A5.d: An ammonia (NH3) sensor behind the SCR catalyst tells the controller whether too much urea is dosed and ammonia slips through. Like NOx sensors it carries its own electronics and talks over CAN; Bosch even offers NOx sensors that add a selective ammonia signal.
s: Check engine light on
Code appears right after an engine software update
SCR dosing runs without ammonia feedback
c: Engine calibration does not match the sensor fit (with or without NH3 sensor)
Damaged wiring or connector at the ammonia sensor

U05A6.d: Diesel exhaust fluid freezes at about -11 °C, and EU rules demanded that it be usable within 20 minutes after a start at -15 °C, so tanks, pumps and lines get electric heaters. Where these heaters are driven by a separate control module, it reports heater states, temperatures and faults to the engine or dosing controller over the bus.
s: Check engine light or DEF system warning
Delayed DEF dosing after cold starts
c: Water or salt corrosion at module connector or bus wiring
Software levels of heater module and engine controller do not fit

U05A7.d: The Safety Integration Control Module appears in the SAE code catalogue, yet no carmaker explains in public what this unit does or which models carry it; the name suggests a controller that ties several safety functions together. U05A7 is stored by a receiving module that still gets the unit's frames but refuses what they contain.
s: Warning message about safety or assistance systems
Individual assistance functions unavailable
Further network codes stored in several modules
c: Software fault or outdated software in the safety integration module
Module replaced or reprogrammed without matching vehicle configuration
Corrupted frames from wiring, connector or termination faults on the bus
Low supply voltage during start or after battery discharge

U05A8.d: A third NOx sensor appears on exhaust systems with two SCR stages, where sensor C watches the gas after the second catalyst. GM's 2025 ECM tables (25OBDG04B) are the public example: the engine controller checks alive rolling count and checksum of the post-second-catalyst NOx signals, eight failures in 18 samples or three in ten depending on the signal, with battery voltage of at least 11 V for 5 s, and logs U05A8 as
s: Check engine light after two trips
SCR monitor for the second catalyst incomplete
c: Control unit of NOx sensor C faulty
Harness or connector of the rearmost sensor damaged
Sensors swapped between positions during repair

U05A9.d: With this code the third NOx sensor, fitted after a second SCR stage, reports that it cannot use the frames the engine controller sends it, such as heater release or operating state. No manufacturer documents U05A9 publicly.
s: Check engine light on
No NOx value from sensor C on the scan tool
c: Intermittent bus connection to sensor C
Engine controller not configured for the third sensor
Sensor C control unit rejecting valid data

U05AA.d: Engines with a water-cooled charge air cooler use an electric pump, often a LIN slave of the engine controller, to move coolant through the low-temperature circuit. CARB requires the charge air cooling to be checked for performance and its electronic parts to be monitored.
s: Check engine light on
Reduced engine power in hot conditions
Coolant warning or radiator fan running at full speed
c: Pushed-out or corroded terminals at the pump connector
Fault elsewhere on the shared LIN bus or in the master module software

U05AB.d: In parallel hybrids the engine disconnect clutch sits between engine crankshaft and electric machine; opened, it lets the car drive electrically with the engine off, closed, it starts the engine or adds its torque. Ford's patents describe the clutch being prestroked so it is filled with pressure before an engine start is requested, and being advanced before the hydraulic pump spins down.
s: Hybrid system warning and check engine light
Electric driving unavailable, engine runs continuously
Jerky engine starts
c: Clutch actuator electronics or position sensor faulty
Actuator and hybrid controller software not matched or adaptation lost
Wiring or connector at the transmission bell housing damaged

U05AC.d: Electrified cars increasingly run cabin, battery and drive-unit cooling from one thermal management controller that commands pumps, valves, fans and the refrigerant circuit; suppliers such as Hirain and Marelli sell such units, Marelli explicitly with OBD compliance. For hybrids, CARB requires the electronic parts used for battery and inverter cooling or heating to be monitored and, where feasible, the cooling perfor
s: Various warning messages in the cluster
Reduced charging or drive power
Climate control not working properly
c: Thermal management controller software out of date
Faulty temperature or pressure sensor feeding the controller

U05B2.d: Stellantis calls its touch screens for climate, seat and similar comfort settings Comfort and Convenience Display Modules (CCDM); the Jeep Grand Wagoneer has one up front and a second one for rear passengers. U05B2 is logged when a receiver gets traffic from display A whose content is implausible.
s: Climate or seat settings change without input
Display shows functions the vehicle does not have
Comfort controls on the screen respond late or not at all
c: Display firmware with known faults, newer part number available
Display configuration not matching vehicle equipment, proxi alignment missing
Touch panel or display electronics defective
Loose or corroded connector at the display

U05B3.d: Display B is the second comfort screen on vehicles fitted with more than one, typically a rear unit from which back-seat occupants adjust climate and seats. U05B3 is set when its frames arrive but do not pass the receiver's validity checks, whereas U02B2 would mean that display B has fallen silent.
s: Rear climate settings change by themselves
Rear comfort screen does not accept inputs
Front display shows rear functions as unavailable
c: Rear comfort display with old firmware sending spurious commands
Replacement display not configured to the vehicle
Chafed or loose wiring to the rear console display

U05B4.d: A driver monitoring system films the driver's face with an infrared camera to judge attention and drowsiness. Toyota launched it in 2006, Cadillac relies on one to allow hands-free Super Cruise, and EU Regulation 2019/2144 covers it.
s: Hands-free or lane assistance not available
Driver attention warning inactive or triggered without reason
Service message for driver assistance in the cluster
c: Low 12 V state of charge or recent battery replacement
Camera or infrared emitters covered, dirty or misaligned
Module software or calibration not matching the ADAS controller

U05B5.d: Front radar modules measure distance and closing speed of objects ahead for adaptive cruise, emergency braking and lane change support. Mercedes-Benz documents this code on the 2026 CLA electric (series 174): the driver assistance controller N62/5 stores U05B555 when the front radar on the outer left delivers implausible data because it has not been configured.
s: Driver assistance unavailable message that does not clear
Adaptive cruise and emergency braking switched off
Lane change or blind spot functions on the front left limited
c: Radar sensor not configured or calibrated in the assistance controller (Mercedes N62/5)
Outdated software in the driver assistance controller
Radar knocked out of alignment after bumper damage or repair
Radar connector behind the bumper loose or wet

U05B6.d: Letter B on a front radar points to different hardware depending on the brand. At Mercedes-Benz, U05B655 on the 2026 CLA electric marks implausible data from the front radar on the outer right, again with sub-code 55 for a sensor that was never configured, and it shares the remedy of the left unit: calibrating control unit N62/5 per LI54.71-P-080345.
s: Adaptive cruise control not available
Forward collision warning switched off
Lane centring or active driving assist not ready
c: Right front radar not configured after production or replacement (Mercedes)
Long-range radar connector not fully latched (Stellantis D1082A)
Radar cover dirty, iced or damaged

U05B7.d: Rear radar modules are hidden in the corners of the rear bumper and feed blind spot warning, rear cross traffic alert and the exit warning that watches for cyclists when a door opens. Mercedes-Benz stores U05B755 on the 2026 CLA electric when the rear radar on the outer left sends implausible data because it is not configured; the driver assistance controller N62/5 then keeps several functions offline.
s: Blind spot indicator on the left stays off
Rear cross traffic and exit warnings unavailable
Assistance unavailable message in the instrument cluster
c: Left rear radar not configured in the assistance controller
Rear bumper repaired or repainted, sensor mount or cover altered
Moisture or corrosion at the rear radar connector

U05B8.d: Module B is the right-hand rear corner radar in the only public manufacturer use: Mercedes-Benz lists U05B855 for the outer right rear sensor of the 2026 CLA electric. The fault type 55 reads as not configured, so the content is rejected because the controller N62/5 has no valid setup for that sensor, not because the radar is broken.
s: Blind spot indicator on the right stays off
Assistance warnings reappear on every start
Rear cross traffic alert missing on the right
c: Right rear radar not configured, calibration of the assistance controller missing
Initial calibration of the controller's acceleration sensor not completed

U05B9.d: A third rear radar is only needed on vehicles whose rear coverage goes beyond the usual pair of corner sensors, for example to watch longer flanks or the area directly behind. No manufacturer publishes U05B9 or the position of a rear radar C, and its lost-communication partner U02B8 has no public bulletin either.
s: Rear assistance warnings partly unavailable
Service message for driver assistance
c: Rear radar C not configured or calibrated after replacement
Sensor position or cover changed by rear body repair
Wiring or connector fault at rear radar C

U05BA.d: Rear radar module D is the fourth unit in the rear numbering and is reserved for layouts with an unusually dense sensor set at the back. Neither U05BA nor the matching lost-communication code U02B9 is described by any manufacturer in public, so there are no published thresholds or fitting positions.
s: Individual rear warnings such as exit warning not available
Assistance message in the instrument cluster
c: Rear radar D not coded to the vehicle
Assistance controller software rejects data from module D

U05BD.d: Hands-free and highly automated driving needs to know the car's position to lane level and the road ahead from a detailed map. GM handles this in a separate map module (K179) for Super Cruise: it holds a LiDAR-surveyed map that decides where the system may be engaged and receives map and GPS correction data over the air while driving.
s: Hands-free driving not offered on mapped roads
Service driver assist message
Lane-level guidance or map-based speed adaptation missing
c: Map database outdated because over-the-air updates could not complete
Poor satellite reception or faulty GNSS antenna and cable
Module software not matching the assistance controller
Localization and mapping module internally defective

U05BE.d: Night vision systems show the road beyond the headlight beam, either passively with a thermal camera that picks up heat from people and animals or actively with near-infrared illumination. The control module processes the picture, detects pedestrians and sends image and warning data to the cluster or head-up display.
s: Night vision image missing or frozen
Pedestrian and animal warnings at night unavailable
Night vision fault message in the cluster
c: Bent pins or loose terminals at the night vision module connector
Infrared camera or its video link delivering faulty data

U05BF.d: Trailer backup assist lets the driver reverse a trailer by turning a knob rather than the wheel; the vehicle measures the hitch angle and steers for the chosen path. Ford's Pro Trailer Backup Assist reads the angle from a target sticker via the rear camera or from a sensor on the trailer, and a Ford patent caps the steering command according to how fast the hitch angle changes, so the rig does not jackknife.
s: Trailer backup assist cannot be activated or cancels
Rear park assist temporarily unavailable
Warning messages in other modules, on some trucks with MIL
c: Internal software fault in the trailer backup assist module
Implausible hitch angle input from trailer target, camera or trailer sensor
Trailer profile incomplete or measured dimensions wrong
Module supply interrupted or connector loose

U05C0.d: Cars with extensive ambient and cabin lighting split it across several controllers; module B is the second of these, for instance for the rear cabin, the doors or a separate light strip, while A runs the main zone. These nodes usually hang on a LIN line below the body controller, which sends them colour and brightness commands and polls their status; Microchip's reference design runs this at about 10.4 kbit/s with a
s: Ambient light zone stays dark or flickers
Wrong colour or brightness in part of the cabin
Lighting settings in the menu not applied to all zones
c: LED controller of lighting module B defective
LIN line or connector to module B damaged, for example in a door hinge area
Replacement module B not configured for its zone

U05C1.d: Besides shutters in the visible grille, some cars meter cooling air with flaps placed directly in front of the radiator, behind the bumper intake. Hyundai's patent US11225900B2 describes such an arrangement with two adjacent flaps between bumper opening and radiator plus an air guide steering air towards them.
s: Warning lamp on some vehicles
Flap stays open, slightly higher consumption
c: Connector behind the bumper wet or corroded
Flap blocked by debris or ice so the actuator reports implausible positions
